name: Coterra Energy Inc.

profile.description: Coterra Energy was an independent oil and gas producer with Marcellus Shale natural gas, Permian Basin and Anadarko Basin assets, formed by the October 2021 merger of Cabot Oil & Gas and Cimarex Energy. FY2025 revenue was $7.65B with $1.72B of net income and $1.63B of free cash flow. Coterra NO LONGER TRADES: its $58B all-stock merger with Devon Energy closed May 7-8, 2026, each CTRA share converted into 0.70 DVN shares, and the stock was delisted from the NYSE (last quote $32.56). This report scores pre-merger metrics for reference only; the investable successor is DVN.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): The 2021 Cabot-Cimarex combination turned a single-basin Marcellus gas producer into a multi-basin oil and gas company, and $3.24B of 2025 acquisitions plus the 2026 Devon merger extended that transformation [3][1]. AI Deployment (0/2): Research found no shipped AI tools or quantified AI-driven savings; the only technology reference was a Chief Technology Officer role [4]. Market Share (1/2): The company remained Pennsylvania's most prolific driller, a meaningful regional position but not a category-defining one [6]. Pipeline (1/2): Pre-merger guidance and the $1B synergy target for the combined company give general visibility, but no named next-generation projects with dates were found [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Coterra reported zero R&D expense in its income statements [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Leadership framed priorities as safety, financial strength and shareholder value creation, which describes what an E&P does rather than a distinctive purpose [4]. Community Impact (0/2): The most visible community spending was the $16.29M public water system funded under the 2022 no-contest criminal plea over methane contamination in Dimock, PA, which is remediation, not voluntary giving [6]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): No net insider buying was identified before the stock was delisted.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Dividend-sleeve calculation on pre-merger TTM data (stock delisted May 2026): D/E 23.2% scores 1.0; ROE 11.0% (derived from FMP TTM net income per share $2.20 / book value per share $19.91) scores 0.74; FY2025 revenue growth of 40.1% and 5-year revenue CAGR of 39.1% (FY2020 $1.47B to FY2025 $7.65B, inflated by the Cimarex merger and 2025 acquisitions) both score 1.0; profit margin 21.7% scores 1.0; forward P/E unavailable and excluded [2][3]. Dividend metrics: payout ratio 40.4% scores 0.99; 6 consecutive documented years of dividends (FY2020-FY2025 cash flow statements) scores 0.6 (2x); dividend per share only grew in 2025 after variable-dividend cuts in 2023-2024, so 1 year of growth scores 0.1; derived 5-year DPS CAGR of ~17.5% ($0.40 to $0.90) scores 1.0 (2x) [5]. Weighted sum 9.03 / 11 = 8. The liquidity floor cannot be applied because there has been no trading since delisting; IOWN cannot buy CTRA.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Drilling, completing and producing hydrocarbons is a physical, permitted, capital-intensive activity that software cannot substitute, and AI data-center power demand supports natural gas demand from Coterra's Marcellus position [1][3]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue or monetized AI products were identified [4].

infinite_game.summary: Coterra was a disciplined capital allocator, but in Sinek's terms it played a finite game: its stated priorities were safety, balance-sheet strength and shareholder value, and its defining strategic acts were two scale-driven mergers, the second of which ended its independent existence. The Dimock grand jury's finding of 'long-term indifference' to local harm is the opposite of a Just Cause lived out.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The company's purpose language centered on safety, financial strength and shareholder value creation, a functional description rather than a vision of a better future [4]. The Dimock record, in which a grand jury criticized Cabot's 'long-term indifference to the damage it caused', undercuts any implicit stewardship cause [6].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Strategic decisions were framed around capital efficiency, buybacks ($141M in 2025) and synergy capture, and the company chose to merge into Devon with a $1B synergy target rather than pursue an independent long-term path [1][5]. No example was found of sacrificing near-term returns for a higher purpose.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CEO Tom Jorden provided leadership continuity, leading Cimarex from 2011 and Coterra from 2021, and publicly credited employees' dedication and professionalism for 2025 results [4]. No retention data was available, and the merger handed the CEO role to Devon's Clay Gaspar [1].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The Cabot-Cimarex merger moved a pure Appalachian gas producer into oil-weighted Permian and Anadarko assets, a real but incremental business-model shift [3]. The final strategic act was a sale-style merger rather than a reinvention.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary acknowledging competitors' strengths as a spur to self-improvement was found; competition was framed around scale and cost position [1].

investment_thesis: CTRA is no longer investable on its own: the Devon merger closed May 7-8, 2026, converting each share into 0.70 DVN shares, and Coterra holders now own about 46% of the combined company [1]. On its final full year, Coterra was financially strong, with FY2025 revenue of $7.65B (+40%), net income of $1.72B, free cash flow of $1.63B, D/E of 23% and a 40% payout ratio [2][3][5]. The combined company targets $1B of annual pre-tax synergies by year-end 2027 and has authorized an $8B buyback through June 2029, which is the value path for former CTRA holders [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case was always commodity exposure and a weak purpose profile. Dividends per share fell from ~$2.50 in 2022 to ~$0.84 in 2024 as variable payouts tracked prices, and FY2025 ended with only $119M of cash after $3.24B of acquisitions [5]. The Dimock contamination case, which produced a 2022 no-contest criminal plea and a $16.29M water-system obligation, is a lasting reputational stain [6]. Any decision should now be made on DVN, which carries the integration risk of a $58B merger and a new CEO.
key_catalysts: Delivery of the combined Devon-Coterra company's $1B annual pre-tax synergy target by year-end 2027, which drives value for former CTRA holders now owning ~46% of DVN [1]
Execution of Devon's $8B share repurchase authorization running through June 30, 2029 [1]
Rising natural gas demand from AI data centers benefiting the legacy Coterra Marcellus acreage inside DVN [3]
key_risks: Ticker delisted May 2026; CTRA cannot be purchased, and screening value now depends entirely on DVN's fundamentals [1]
Commodity price volatility, shown by dividends per share falling ~66% from 2022 to 2024 under the variable-dividend framework [5]
Integration and leadership-change risk in a $58B all-stock merger with a new CEO and an 11-member blended board [1]
